title: Redwood Centralized Controls Handbook — Access, Change, Data, Procurement & Travel
author: Ava Nguyen
body:
Overview

This handbook consolidates company-wide operating controls that touch multiple teams: Access & Permissions, Change Management, Data Management, Procurement & Expenses, Vendor Management, and Travel. It provides standards, decision criteria, and ready-to-use templates for day-to-day operations and audit readiness. Owners and approvers are explicitly identified for each area.

Intended audience
- Team leads and managers
- People Ops and Finance partners
- Security and Compliance
- Service owners making product or infra changes

Principles
- Least privilege by default; explicit exceptions are documented and time-bound.
- Changes must be risk-assessed, peer-reviewed, and reversible.
- Data classification drives retention, access, and protection controls.
- Procurement follows a three-tier approval matrix based on dollar thresholds and vendor risk.

1) Access & Permissions
Purpose: ensure consistent account lifecycle, role definitions, and periodic review.
Owners: People Ops (lifecycle), Security (policy/risk), Team Managers (approvers).

Key controls:
- Role catalog: every team must publish a minimal role-to-permission mapping in the team wiki (owner: team lead).
- Onboarding: access requests must be opened via the Access Request template (see below) and approved by manager + security for privileged roles.
- Offboarding: accounts disabled within 4 business hours of termination notice; credentials rotated if account held shared resources.
- Privileged access (KMS, production consoles): require MFA, approved JIT windows, and session logging.
- Quarterly access review: managers must confirm current members/roles for each repo, service, and cloud account. Audit evidence: review comments in the access system.

Access request template (YAML - copy into ticket):

---
requester: "<name>"
email: "<user@redwood.ai>"
team: "<team>"
role: "<role-name>"
resource: "<service/repo/cloud-project>"
justification: "<business-justification and duration>"
approvers: ["manager","security"]
expiration: "YYYY-MM-DD (optional)"
---

Approval windows and SLAs:
- Standard requests: 48 hours target approval.
- Privileged roles: 5 business days (security review).

2) Change Management
Purpose: reduce downtime and risk from infrastructure, model, and application changes.
Owners: Eng Platform (process owner), Service Owners (submitters), Eng SRE (approvers for infra changes).

Change categories and requirements:
1. Standard (low risk): routine configuration or non-prod deploys. Requires owner sign-off and automated tests.
2. Significant (medium risk): production behavior changes, model weight updates, or schema migrations. Requires change ticket, runbook, rollback plan, and peer review.
3. Major (high risk): infra topology changes, multi-region failover, migrations that can cause data loss. Requires change advisory board (CAB) review, scheduled window, and tabletop rehearsal.

Change request checklist (numbered steps):
1) Create change ticket with summary, impact matrix, test plan, and rollback steps.
2) Link associated alerts and dashboards.
3) Assign approvers: service owner + SRE + product if customer-facing.
4) Conduct pre-change validation in staging.
5) During window: log start/end times, contingencies executed, and take sequence snapshots.
6) Post-change: run smoke tests, validate metrics for 2x SLA window, and post a short change report.

SLOs & windows:
- Emergency changes: phone-first escalation, postmortem required within 72 hours.
- Normal maintenance windows: weekday 02:00–06:00 UTC where possible.

3) Data Management & Retention
Purpose: ensure data is classified, retained, and protected per business and regulatory needs.
Owners: Data Governance (policy), Service Owners (local retention), Security (encryption & access controls).

Classification tiers (examples):
- Public: non-sensitive, shareable. Retention: up to 7 years unless specified.
- Internal: business operational data. Retention: default 3 years.
- Confidential: PII, financials, customer data. Retention: per contract/regulatory requirement, minimum 1 year.
- Restricted: data requiring encryption-at-rest and strict access (KMS/HSM keys). Retention: aligned to legal hold.

Retention table (guidance):
- Logs (infra): 90 days hot, 1 year cold (default).
- Audit trails (auth, admin actions): 3 years.
- Customer records: per contract, default 7 years.
- Research model checkpoints: 1 year unless tagged for longer-term reproducibility.

Data handling requirements:
- Use approved storage classes for restricted data; encrypt with company KMS.
- Production datasets moved to non-production must be anonymized or use synthetic substitutes.
- Data access approvals are recorded and time-bound.

4) Procurement, Expenses & Vendor Management
Purpose: ensure financial controls, vendor risk assessment, and timely reimbursements.
Owners: Finance (procurement gating), Procurement Ops (workflows), Hiring/People Ops (travel/expense policies).

Approval matrix (dollar thresholds):
- Low: <$5,000 — Manager approval (PO optional).
- Medium: $5,000–$50,000 — Manager + Finance approver.
- High: >$50,000 — Director-level + Legal and Finance endorsements; requires vendor risk review.

Vendor risk checklist:
- Vendor profile and country of operation.
- Security posture: SOC2 / ISO27001 or compensating controls.
- Data handling: contract language for data residency, encryption, and breach notification.
- Financial diligence and references.
- Termination & transition plan and IP ownership clauses.

Expense guidelines (summary):
- Reimbursements submitted within 30 days.
- Per diem capped at local market rates; receipts required for lodging and airfare.
- Corporate card use prioritized for business travel; personal card reimbursements require manager validation.

Vendor onboarding steps (numbered):
1) Business sponsor raises vendor request with scope and budget.
2) Procurement Ops runs vendor risk checklist and engages Legal for template contract.
3) Finance confirms accounting codes, PO issued per threshold.
4) Contract signed and vendor added to approved vendor registry.
4) Training or integration kickoff scheduled.

Template: Purchase request (JSON example to paste into procurement form):
{
  "requestor": "<name>",
  "business_unit": "<team>",
  "vendor": "<vendor name>",
  "estimated_amount": "<USD>",
  "justification": "<business justification>",
  "approval_chain": ["manager","finance","legal (if >50k)"]
}

5) Travel & Business Travel Policy
Purpose: balance traveler safety, cost control, and business needs.
Owners: People Ops (policy), Facilities (arrangements), Finance (billing).

Key points:
- Booking: employees should use the corporate travel portal for flights and hotels where available.
- Class: domestic flights economy; transcontinental >6 hours may use premium economy with manager pre-approval.
- Safety: use approved travel risk tool for high-risk locations; pre-clearance required for restricted countries.
- Insurance: business travel insurance will be applied for approved trips.
- Approvals: travel requests >$3,000 require Director sign-off; trips including international travel require manager + People Ops notification.

Incident escalation while traveling:
1) If safety incident: contact local emergency services then People Ops on-call.
2) For lost/stolen corporate devices: notify Security and People Ops within 24 hours.

Templates and artifacts (copyable)
- Access request (YAML): (see Access section)
- Change request summary (markdown):
  - Title:
  - Owner:
  - Risk level:
  - Rollback plan:
  - Test plan:
- Vendor intake form (CSV headers): vendor_name, contact_email, country, primary_service, estimated_annual_spend, soc2_status, legal_template_required

Governance and Audit readiness
- Annual control self-assessment: each team completes the Control Self-Assessment (CSA) and uploads artifacts to the compliance drive.
- Evidence retention: approvals, access reviews, and procurement POs are retained for a minimum of 3 years (longer where contracts or laws require).
- Internal audit cadence: Finance & Legal coordinate an annual vendor audit and quarterly spot checks for high-risk vendors.

Ownership matrix (roles as comma-separated list):
- People Ops: onboarding/offboarding lifecycle, travel policy, employee benefits coordination
- Security: privileged access policy, encryption standards, incident response for data breaches
- Finance: procurement approvals, expense policies, vendor payments
- Eng Platform: change process owner, release windows, runbook requirements

Exceptions and risk acceptance
- All exception requests must use the Exception Request template and include compensating controls and an explicit expiry. Risk acceptance is logged and signed by the owning director and Security.

Change log and review cadence
- This handbook is considered a living document. Major reviews scheduled annually; interim updates when policy or regulation changes occur.
- Revision notes: 2024-06: tightened privileged access windows; 2024-11: added vendor risk checklist enhancements; 2025-01: clarified procurement thresholds and travel pre-approval rules.

Appendix: Quick checklists
- Pre-onboarding: manager submits access request, assigns mentor, and schedules security orientation.
- Pre-change: link runbook, smoke tests, and rollback executed in staging.
- Pre-purchase: confirm budget code, vendor risk status, and PO requirement.
